seoTitle: What Happens When You Link a Credit Card to PayPal
metaDescription: Understand what actually changes when you link a credit card to PayPal, including verification, fees, payment processing, and buyer protections.
intro: Linking a credit card to PayPal changes more than just what shows up in your wallet — it affects how payments are processed, verified, and protected. This guide explains what actually happens behind the scenes when you connect a card so you know what to expect.

steps.heading: See what happens when you link a card
steps.body: Once linked, your credit card becomes an available funding source PayPal can use for payments, either automatically or as a backup to your balance.

steps.heading: Understand card verification
steps.body: PayPal typically verifies a newly linked card through a small temporary charge or confirmation code to ensure the card is valid and belongs to you.

steps.heading: Check whether PayPal charges a fee for linking
steps.body: Linking the card itself is generally free, though transaction fees may apply depending on the type of payment made using that card.

steps.heading: Learn how PayPal uses your card for payments
steps.body: Depending on your settings, PayPal may pull funds from the linked card automatically when your balance isn't sufficient to cover a payment.

steps.heading: Know your protections when paying through PayPal
steps.body: Payments made through PayPal using a linked card can benefit from PayPal's buyer protection policies, separate from your card issuer's own protections.

faq.question: Does PayPal charge a fee just for linking a card?
faq.answer: No, linking a card to your PayPal account is typically free; fees usually apply to specific transactions rather than the linking process itself.

faq.question: How does PayPal verify a newly linked credit card?
faq.answer: PayPal often verifies a card through a small temporary charge or a confirmation code sent to your statement, which you then enter to confirm ownership.

faq.question: What happens if my linked card gets declined?
faq.answer: If the card is declined during a payment, PayPal will typically prompt you to try another funding source or resolve the issue with your card issuer.

faq.question: Can I remove a linked card later without issues?
faq.answer: Yes, though removal can be blocked if the card is tied to an active subscription or pending payment, similar to standard card removal on PayPal.
